This would be amazing if I could see it. I really hope the Moon is visible right now!

I'm in Alice Springs, Australia at 2026-11-10 18:27 ACST (UTC+0930) (2026-11-10T08:57:00Z in UTC), at latitude -23.698 degrees and longitude 133.8807 degrees. My astronomy app says the Sun's altitude is 5.086 degrees and its azimuth is 253.378 degrees, so it is above the horizon. It says the Moon's altitude is 16.793 degrees and its azimuth is 249.764 degrees, so it is above the horizon. The Moon is 1.32 percent illuminated, 13.169 degrees from the Sun, and 398861.4 kilometers away. The sky brightness is bright daylight, the sky is clear, and I'm an ordinary adult with normal unaided eyesight who knows roughly where to look.

Do you think I'd actually be able to spot it?

Probably not—at least not with unaided eyesight under those conditions.

The Moon is technically above the horizon, but it is an extremely thin crescent: only **1.32% illuminated** and just **13.2° from the Sun**. With the Sun still **5.1° above the horizon**, the sky will remain very bright, and the crescent’s illuminated portion will be close to the Sun’s direction—making it strongly washed out by glare and atmospheric brightness.

Its altitude of **16.8°** is favorable enough geometrically, but the key issue is contrast, not position. An experienced observer might detect it with binoculars or a telescope—while taking great care never to point them near the Sun—but an ordinary observer with unaided vision is very unlikely to see it. Wait until after sunset, when the Sun is below the horizon, and the crescent may become visible briefly in the western sky, though it will set fairly soon afterward.
